macro_context: Buying and selling used chemical process plants and equipment
primary_keyword: used chemical process plants for sale
content_type: Commercial collection page, two-sided (buyer and seller)

transactional.buyer: Acquire a listed plant or unit: open IMS listings, filter, search a stock number, request a quotation or an inspection.
transactional.seller: Sell a plant or surplus equipment to IPP: send the asset list through the sell-a-plant or sell-equipment form, or contact IPP.

commercial.buyer: Evaluate before acquiring: equipment types and their values, makers, IPP's advantages, how buying works, customer proof, FAQs.
commercial.seller: Evaluate IPP as the buyer of a site or surplus asset: what IPP acquires, how selling works, decommissioning credentials, projects, seller FAQs.

intent_model.page_primary_intent: Transactional (buy) led, with a co-equal transactional seller path; commercial sections support both decisions

audience_type: Buyers: procurement, engineering and operations teams at chemical producers. Sellers: plant owners and asset managers with shutdown, idled or surplus assets.
commercial_orientation: Buyer-led page with a co-equal seller path
sentence_form: Every sentence is a subject-predicate-object triple: a named subject (IPP, the plant, the unit, the seller), one single positive verb, and an object carrying the attribute value. No phrasal predicates, no vague quantifiers, no em dashes.
template: Mode B. The user's Suggested Outline (workbook tab) plus the tracker sections already on the review page. Arrangement follows the live reactor hub: hero triples, listings, browse by type, makers, advantages, process, industries, FAQ, call to action; adjusted so the seller path mirrors the buyer path.
constraints: Existing URL and canonical stay; H1 stays 'Used Chemical Process Plants for Sale'
'How buying from IPP works' copy stays exactly as published (user lock)
Preserved original sentences stay word for word (hero sentence 1, seven category descriptions, three FAQ answers, six industries)

Approved claim lines only: up to 50% of capital and 90% of lead time versus buying new; the exact-savings sentence; GPS 12 to 16 week average delivery; since 1980
